about: Make's tools for agents (through Agent Link): name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

fit.description: Give sizes for parts that fit together, and keep the fit calibration of the printer. action: size when left out. size { nominal mm (the size of the bought or mating part), of: hole|shaft (hole when left out), kind: press|snug|slide|free (all four when left out), body } gives the diameter to MODEL. A hole is nominal + the gap of the fit + what this printer prints a hole small. A shaft is nominal − what it prints a peg big. The gap of the fit is always put on the hole. calibrate { hole, shaft } keeps with the document how much this printer prints a hole small and a peg big. The values are diametral mm, each −1 to 1; hole 0.2 and shaft 0 when left out. Every later size, hw_hole and hw_embed takes it. stack { items: [{ name, nominal (signed mm), tol (± mm) }], target: [lo, hi] } adds a tolerance stack. Gotchas: with no calibration kept, the hole allowance is 0.2 mm, and printerFit says so. The fit of the print setup of a body wins over the fit of the document (body picks the setup). calibrate writes a record, though the tool is listed as a read. That record is not an undo step. The answer holds: size { of, nominal, model { kind: mm }, printerFit }; calibrate { calibration { hole, shaft }, note }; stack { nominal, worstCase [lo, hi], rss [lo, hi], worstCaseOk, rssOk (with target) }.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

fit.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

hw_hole.description: Make a hole for hardware in a body. kind: clearance | counterbore | countersink | nut_trap, insert (heat-set) or magnet. size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6 or M8; M3 when left out; insert takes the same sizes. fit: close|normal|loose is ISO 273 fine|medium|coarse. magnet size: "6x2", diameter x thickness mm. at [x, y, z] in document coordinates is where the hole ENTERS, on a flat face. dir runs INTO the material ("-z" when left out; "+x", "-y" … or [x, y, z]). depth: mm or "through" (the default). Insert and magnet pockets take their own depth. The head side (screw head, counterbore, countersink, nut trap) is always on the face that at is on. headSide says which ("countersink on the face at x=0, facing -x"). For a wall bracket, enter from the face away from the wall. In a PartDesign Body, it is FreeCAD's own PartDesign Hole on a new sketch on that face. The Hole is editable in its panel. features lists them: HoleSketch, Hole, and for a nut trap NutTrapSketch + NutTrap, a Pocket. face: the entry face, instead of finding it from at and dir. face is "Face6" (on the tip of the Body) or "Pocket.Face4" (of a feature). Face numbers change after any edit, so pick the face again (shape_query); do not reuse one. sketch: a sketch in the Body whose circle centres are the holes (at not needed; not for nut_trap). Printer allowance: the fit calibration of the print setup or the document (fit calibrate) is added to the diameters. When none is kept, the allowance is 0.2 mm. With an allowance, the Hole is FreeCAD's plain hole (ThreadType None) at the ISO 273 size + allowance. That is because FreeCAD sets the Diameter of a sized hole again from size and fit on every reopen. The size it stands for is in the Label2 of the Hole, and allowanceOn names the properties. A size picked later in the own panel of the Hole loses the allowance: run hw_hole again instead. Other bodies: a plain Part solid (Part::Feature) is cut as a shape (route "Part solid", not editable). A parametric Part object (a Part::Box, a boolean, an extrusion) is refused. FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the hole. The refusal names the plain copy (part_transform copy) or pd_clone to use. The Body is recomputed first; a broken last feature is refused by name. Each call is one hole, or the holes of one sketch. The answer holds { body, kind, size, sizes, printerFit, allowance, depth, through, removed, route, features, headSide (+ face, facing), note, sound (+ problems), step }. through: mm of material passed. removed: mm³. route: "PartDesign Hole" | "Part solid". sizes holds those that apply: freecadSize, fit, clearance, clearanceBeforeAllowance, cut, cutDiameter, cutDepth, nutAcrossFlats, nutDepth, hole, depth. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. More: guide_read { topic: "hole" }.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

face.description: The entry face on the Body's tip, e.g. Face6 (PartDesign Body only).

sketch.description: A sketch in the Body whose circles are the holes' centres (PartDesign Body only; at not needed).

hw_hole.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

thread_lookup.description: Read thread sizes in mm from FreeCAD's own PartDesign Hole tables (ISO metric coarse and fine, UNC, UNF). It reads the tables once a session. size: "M6", "M10x1.25", "1/4-20", "#10-32"; a bare "1/4" is the coarse one. With size, the answer holds thread { size, series, major, pitch, pitchDia, minorInt, minorExt, tapDrill, freecad, source, insert { hole, depth, source }, tpi, tapDrillName }. freecad: the name that FreeCAD's Hole lists it by. insert: where there are heat-set insert figures. tpi and tapDrillName: for Unified sizes. Without size: a table for series metric | metric-fine | unc | unf | all (all when left out). near: a diameter in mm; it keeps the six sizes whose major is nearest. The answer then holds threads [{ size, major, pitch, minorInt, tapDrill }], columns, source. Gotchas: pitch diameter and minors are worked out from the ISO 68-1 basic profile, not read from FreeCAD. FreeCAD gives no Unified pitch. So a Unified size that FreeCAD lists, but that Workshop has no threads-per-inch for, has pitch null. A size that is not listed is refused not_found. Your own sizes go in ~/.config/workshop_make/threads.json. Changes nothing.
thread_lookup.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

thread_identify.description: Find what thread a hole or shaft is. faces: the cylindrical wall, by query. Give { near: [x, y, z] }: a point on or beside it; only cylindrical faces are looked at. Or give { faces: ["Face7"] }: face numbers change after any edit. body: when there is more than one. The answer holds: body, face, diameter, kind (hole | shaft), length, axis, nearest [{ size, series, pitch, as, standard, off (mm from it) }], best, alsoPicked. as: a hole is read as tapDrill, minor or major; a shaft as major. When sizes tie but for pitch (M10, M10x1.25, M10x1), the answer has needs: "pitch" and ask instead of best. Then ask the person or measure, and call again with pitch mm. A note says when the nearest is over 0.3 mm off. That is a clearance hole or a press fit, not a thread. scan: { axis: { element } | { origin, direction, radius }, band, length, pitchFloor } reads a scanned thread instead. scan finds pitch, starts, hand, flank and the standard it matches; families narrows them. scan works only with ScanRuler-FreeCAD installed (its scan_thread); else it is refused unavailable. Changes nothing; thread_cut threads the hole.

faces.description: The cylindrical face by query: { near: [x,y,z] } (cylindrical faces only) or { faces: ["Face7"] }

scan.description: As scan_thread takes: { axis: { element } | { origin, direction, radius }, band, length, pitchFloor }.

thread_identify.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

thread_cut.description: Thread an existing hole with FreeCAD's PartDesign Hole. faces (required): the cylindrical wall of the hole, { near: [x, y, z] } or { faces: ["Face7"] }. Face numbers change after any edit. size: "M6", "M10x1.25", "1/4-20". Left out, size is the nearest standard size. That is refused when two sizes fit alike, or when none is within 0.3 mm. mode cosmetic (default): the hole is drilled to the tapping size, and the thread is recorded with the document. Tap it after you make the part. mode modelled: the helix is cut into the part. It is slow, a second or more per turn, and it gives many faces. Keep it for coarse threads that will be printed, M5 and up. depth: mm (the length of the hole when left out). from [x, y, z]: which end to start at. Left out, it is the open end, the upper one of two. In a PartDesign Body, the thread is a real feature that stays, editable in the panel of the Hole. The feature is a sketch at the end of the hole (ThreadSketch) and a PartDesign Hole. The Hole has Thread and Threaded, and ModelThread for modelled. route is "PartDesign Hole", and features names them. In a plain Part solid (Part::Feature), the Hole is made in a scratch Body. The result is written back as a plain shape (route "Part solid"). A parametric Part object (Part::Box, a boolean …) is refused, since FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the thread. The refusal names the plain copy or pd_clone. A shaft (outside thread) is recorded cosmetic only: FreeCAD threads holes, not shafts. Refused: the hole is already over the major diameter of the thread. Refused: the size is one of your own that FreeCAD's Hole does not list. A modelled thread in a body in a print setup takes the 3D-print clearance of Fasteners Workbench. That is when Fasteners Workbench is installed (printClearance). The answer holds: thread { body, size, series, mode, kind, diameter, depth, at, into, holeDiameter, feature }, removed (mm³), sound (+ problems), route, features, step, note, warning, warning2. warning: modelled under M5 in a print. warning2: the hole was wider than the tap drill. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

faces.description: The cylindrical face by query: { near: [x,y,z] } (cylindrical faces only) or { faces: ["Face7"] }

thread_cut.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

hw_embed.description: Encase a bought part mid-print. It cuts a closed pocket for the part inside a body that is in a print setup. It records the pause to drop the part in. kind nut: size M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8. kind magnet: "6x2", diameter x thickness. kind bearing: 623, 624, 625, 626, 608, 688, 6000, 6001, MR105, MR85, or "22x7" (outer diameter x width). kind insert: M2…M8. kind weight: size "20x8" round or "30x20x6" box, or dims. kind box: dims [w, d, h]. kind cylinder: dims [diameter, h]. at [x, y, z] (required, document coordinates): the centre of the FLOOR of the pocket, inside the material. The part stands upright (+z); turn is ° about z. fit: press|snug|slide|free (slide: drops in by hand), with the fit calibration of the printer. headroom: mm over the part (0.2). The top of the pocket is rounded up to the layer grid of the setup. The pause comes after that layer. Refused: no print setup (setup add first). Refused: the pocket would come out of the part. Refused: no material over it (use hw_hole for a pocket pressed in after). Refused: the roof is under 2 layers or minRoof mm. The pocket is written into the body as a plain shape. So the body must be a plain Part solid (Part::Feature): gen_make's, an import, a part_transform copy. A PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make. FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the pocket. Trap: the part goes in from above, so nothing may overhang the pocket at the pause. +z is the print direction. The answer holds: body, id (E1 …), what, pocket { shape, size, depth, floor, top (mm from the bed) }, pause { afterLayer, z, note }, roof, least { roof, wall }, sides, printerFit, step, warning. sides: the least wall beside or under it. warning: when sides is under the least wall. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. More: guide_read { topic: "embed" }.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

hw_embed.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

hw_embed_list.description: List the parts encased in a body (the records of hw_embed). The answer holds: embeds [{ id, what, pocket (its sizes mm), floor and top (mm from the bed), layer (the pause comes after it), roof (mm of material over it), note }]. A record whose pocket is solid again (an undo, or a later edit filled it) is dropped from the list. It is named under dropped { ids, why }. body: you can leave it out when there is one. Reads; only the dropping of dead records is written.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

hw_embed_list.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

hw_unembed.description: Take an encased part out again, by its id (hw_embed_list gives them). The pocket is filled back to solid, and its pause is dropped. keepPocket: true leaves the pocket as an open hole (the part pressed in after printing) and drops only the pause. Filling writes a plain shape, so as with hw_embed, the body must be a plain Part solid. An id that is not there is refused, with a list of those that are. The answer holds: body, removed (the id), pocket ("filled" | "left open …"), solids, step. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

hw_unembed.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

hw_pauses.description: List every pause that the print of a body needs, on the layer grid of its print setup. The answer holds: pauses [{ afterLayer (1 is the first layer), z (mm from the bed: the top of that layer), ids, note (what goes in), merged (two on one layer made one) }], count, layerHeight, firstLayer. It counts the pockets of hw_embed and the magnets of gen_make (id gen_make). The pockets of mass_ballast are not in this list; its own answer gives pauseAt. Refused: the body is in no print setup. slice and slice_with write these pauses into the G-code. Changes nothing, but it drops records whose pocket is gone (dropped).

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

hw_pauses.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

setup.description: Record how each part is made, with the document. The records are a hidden object, saved in the .FCStd and undone with the rest. action: list when left out. list → setups [{ id (S1 …), type, name, bodies, its settings }] and types (the settings of each type, explained). of { body } → the setup of that body, or none. add { type: print|cut|mill, bodies: [names], settings, name } → added. bodies can name a mesh too, for slice_with. set { id (or the name of the setup), bodies (replaces the list) | add: [names] | remove: [names], settings, name } → setup. In set, a settings value of null drops that setting. remove { id } → removed. Print settings: printer (generic, bed-slinger, corexy, h2d), nozzle mm, layerHeight, firstLayer, walls, infill %, topLayers, bottomLayers. For print, up is +z only; slicer_presets use sets slicerPresets. Cut settings: machine (laser, waterjet, plasma, router), thickness, kerf, material, sheet [w, h]. The setup keeps a common machine name as its machine (fiber laser and CO2 laser are laser). It refuses a machine or a sheet material that cut_check does not take, and gives the list. Mill settings: axes "3" | "3+2", minTool, grade (IT 5–14), directions, material, stock [x, y, z], reach. Gotchas: a body is in at most one setup of a type. add refuses it, naming the setup set { remove } to run first. Bodies are recorded by Label, so a body renamed afterwards drops out of its setup; set { add } it again. An unknown setting is refused with the list. A body in no setup has no process, and nothing here guesses one. Ask the person, then add. dfm_check, slice, hw_embed, cut_check and mill_check read the setup. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

setup.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

part_spec.description: Keep with the document the limits that every part of it must meet, and what parts are made of. spec { minWall mm, massMin g, massMax g, minSafety, minClearance mm }. minSafety is a safety factor, judged against the last fea_solve. Each given key is set, null drops it, and clear: true starts from none. Anything else is refused. Called with nothing, it answers what is kept. material: a printing filament id (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a) for bodies [names]. bodies is the one body when left out; material "" forgets theirs. It also puts FreeCAD's own material card on the body, where one matches (freecadMaterial). For any other material (metals, woods, FreeCAD's library), use material_set. Gotchas: the spec is one for the whole document, not per body. Materials are kept by body Label. The answer holds: spec, materials { label: id }, freecadMaterial { label: { card } | { note } }. part_review judges a body against the spec. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.
part_spec.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

dfm_check.description: Check if a body is printable as it stands, +z up, with the nozzle and printer of its print setup. It reads the body in its own frame, +z of the body up, as modelled. A Placement, such as the pose of an assembly, is left out; frame in the answer says so. Bed contact and tall-thin use that frame. In no setup, it uses a 0.4 mm nozzle on a generic printer. It checks thin walls: under one line is an error; under two lines or 0.8 mm is a warning. It checks overhangs past 50° from vertical, and flat ceilings over 10 mm (bridges). A ceiling over a pocket of hw_embed is no bridge: after the pause the part in it carries the layers. It comes back under carried, as "carried by E1 after the pause". It checks upright holes too small to print open, and too little bed contact. It checks tall and thin parts (over 8:1), the build volume, and FreeCAD's Check Geometry. The answer holds: body, setup, frame, verdict, findings, carried, wall { least mm, at, read (how many rays), by }, rules (the limits used). findings [{ id (F1 …, worst first), rule (thin-wall, overhang, bridge, small-hole, bed-contact, tall-thin, build-volume, check-geometry), severity, value, limit, unit, at [x, y, z], areaMm2, says (what to do), waived }]. waive { id, reason } accepts on purpose one finding of the LAST dfm_check of that body. Run the check first: ids are per check. The waiver is kept with the document, and that rule at that place comes back waived from then on. Heavy on detailed bodies (rays against every face): it runs as a job when long. An answer with a job id is finished with job_status. Walls are sampled by rays, so a thin spot between samples can be missed. view_render can draw the wall map (view_maps lists the maps). Listed as a read: waive writes its record without an undo step. part_review folds this check into one verdict. verdict: the check in a few words, from the findings not waived ("printable", "printable, 2 warnings", "not printable: 1 problem, 1 warning"). Agent Link's Activity tab and caption show these words for the call.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

dfm_check.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

part_review.description: Give one verdict on a part: pass, fix or unknown. Run it after every change. It checks soundness (one valid closed solid), then what its setup decides. In a print setup, the findings of the printability check count. That check reads the body in its own frame, as dfm_check does (frame). In no setup, they come under ifPrinted, for information. In a cut or mill setup, they are skipped; cut_check and mill_check judge those. It judges the least wall and the mass against the spec that part_spec keeps. Or give spec { minWall, massMin, massMax } here, for this review only. In a print setup, the mass is as printed: walls, skins and infill, an estimate. Encased magnets, ballast and embeds are counted. minSafety is judged against the last fea_solve of this body, if it is not stale. material: an id for this review only (the body's own, else PLA). waive: [{ rule, at [x, y, z], reason }] accepts a place on purpose; it is kept, and written without an undo step. The answer holds: body, process (printed | cut | mill | unknown), processFrom, verdict, findings [{ source, severity, says, at }], figures { volume, mass, material, as, encasedMass, safety, wall }, frame, carried, checks, spec, ifPrinted, unjudged, printing { pauses }. findings: the first 8, errors first. checks: what ran or was skipped, and why. unjudged: limits that could not be judged; these make the verdict unknown. Heavy on detailed bodies: it runs as a job when long (job_status finishes it). unknown is not pass: read unjudged and supply what is missing.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

material.description: pla (default), petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a

part_review.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

slice.description: Slice a body that is in a print setup with the slicer on this computer. It writes G-code to the folder of the session. With the presets of the person on the setup (slicer_presets use), their slicer slices it (as slice_with). Otherwise PrusaSlicer's command line slices it, with the layer height, nozzle, walls and infill of the setup. AGENTLINK_SLICER names another binary. When PrusaSlicer is absent, it uses OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio, whichever is here; note says so. It needs Agent Link for OrcaSlicer installed, which holds the command lines of the slicers. When that is not installed, it is refused unavailable, saying how to get it. settings { … } overrides the settings of the setup for this slice. name: the base name of the file (the label of the body when left out). pauseCommand (M601) is written before the first layer over each encased part (hw_embed, the magnets of gen_make). pauseCommand: only M601, M600, M0, M1 or PAUSE, one command, no new lines. Other text is refused. material: a filament id (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a) for this slice only, not recorded. Left out, material is the body's own. Refused: the body is in no print setup; the refusal gives the setup add call. Refused: its material is not a printing filament (a metal, a wood); the refusal names material_set and the one-off material. The body is meshed at 0.01 mm deviation first. That takes seconds for a simple part, and a minute or more and a large STL for a detailed one. It runs as a job when long (job_status). The answer holds { body, slicer, gcode, bytes, time, filament, layers, verdict, setup, pauses, material, note }. gcode: the path. filament (g, mm) and layers: as the slicer reports them. material: when given. verdict: a few words with its time and filament ("12m 3s, 3.21 g"), else "G-code written". Starting a print is the call of the person (printer_send).

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

material.description: A filament id (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a, or one of the person's own filaments) for this slice only (not recorded); left out, the body's own material.

slice.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

mass_calibrate.description: Calibrate mass to a weighed print. grams: what the finished print weighed, with anything encased in it, for a body. Every later mass reading is then scaled to match (mass_properties, mass_target, mass_ballast). This applies to bodies in the same print setup. For a body in no print setup, it applies to bodies of the same material. Kept with the document; reset: true drops it. Refused: grams is missing, or under what is encased. Refused: the weight is under 0.3 or over 3 times the estimate. Then it is not the same part and settings: check the body, its setup and its material. The answer holds: calibrated (the key: setup:S1 or solid:<material>), scale, expected (g, before), weighed, encased, for, note. reset answers reset and was. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.
mass_calibrate.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

mass_properties.description: Read the mass, centre of mass and inertia of each body in its material. body: one body; every body shown when left out. In a print setup, the mass is as printed: walls, top and bottom skins and infill. That is an estimate; the figure of the slicer from slice is closer. Else the body is weighed solid. Encased parts are counted: the magnets of gen_make and ballast cut by mass_ballast. A calibration from mass_calibrate is applied. A body with no material is taken as PLA and says so. material_set or part_spec { material } gives it one. The answer holds: bodies [{ body, mass g, com [x, y, z] mm, volume mm³, material, materialId, density g/cm³, as (how it was weighed), inertia { aboutCom 3x3 g·mm², principal }, encased [{ what, count, mass }], bodyMass }], units, hardware, note, printedNote. hardware: Fasteners Workbench screws, listed apart, in steel. Coordinates are the document's. Changes nothing.
mass_properties.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

mass_target.description: Read how far a body is from a target. mass: g (over 0). com: [x, y, z] mm, with null for an axis that does not matter (for example [null, null, 10]). At least one is needed. massTol g and comTol mm (0.5 each) decide met. The answer holds: body, now { mass, com }, mass { target, off, offPct }, com { target, off, distance }, met, and what would get there. Too light: ballast { mass, centre, insideBody, note }. centre is where the centre of one ballast must sit to meet both targets. Too heavy: remove { mass }; ballast only adds. Only the centre off: moment { needed g·mm }. Mass is as mass_properties weighs it (as printed in a print setup). Changes nothing; mass_ballast lays the pockets out.

com.description: [x, y, z] mm; null for an axis that does not matter

mass_target.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

mass_ballast.description: Lay out closed, upright (+z), round ballast pockets inside a body. They reach a target mass g and/or move the centre of mass (com [x, y, z], null for a free axis). At least one is needed. fill: steel-bb (7.85), lead (11.3), tungsten (18), or a density in g/cm³. packing: the share of a pocket that the fill takes, 0.1–1 (0.6 loose shot, 1 a cast slug). diameter: mm (8, at least 2). minWall: mm kept clear of every surface (the minWall of the spec, else 1.2; at least 0.4). maxPockets: 12. Without cut, it only plans (cut: false in the answer, and nothing changed). Read the plan, then call again with cut: true to cut them in one undo step. mass_properties then counts the fill. cut writes a plain shape, so the body must be a plain Part solid (Part::Feature). A PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make. Refused: the body already weighs the target or more. Refused: the fill is no denser than the part as made. Refused: no room for a pocket (use a smaller diameter or wall). Refused: over 600 places to try (use a larger diameter). Cost: every candidate place is probed up the height of the body, then checked whole against the body. That takes a few seconds on a detailed body. cut: true took 26 s on a plate with ten pockets; it weighs the cut body as printed. The pockets are searched greedily, so it is not always exact. massOff and comOff say how close it got. The answer holds: body, fill { what, density, packing, pocketDensity }, pockets [{ at (the floor's centre), diameter, depth, fill g }], before and after { mass, com }, fillMass, minWall, leftOut { places, why }, massOff, comOff, printing { pauseAt mm, note }, cut, sound, step, next. leftOut: places not used, because a hole or pocket of the part runs through the pocket or its wall there. Each pocket and its wall are checked to be all material. printing: pause there, fill, and print over; hw_pauses does not list it. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

com.description: [x, y, z] mm; null for an axis that does not matter

mass_ballast.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f705f4 (moved to Workshop Make)

slicer_presets.description: Read and use the slicer presets of the person, as data. slicer: bambustudio (default) | orcaslicer. action: list when left out. list { slicer, kind: machine|process|filament, query, limit } → the presets on this computer by kind, and saved bundles. Each kind holds { count, own, presets, more }. count: all of that kind that match. own: how many are the person's own. presets: the person's own first, each { name, own: true }, then the names of the others, limit of them. limit is 10 when neither kind nor query is given, else 50. limit 0 gives the counts and the person's own only. more: how many are not shown. kind, query or a higher limit (up to 500) shows them; nothing is out of reach. from (the preset folders read) and next come on the first list of each slicer in a session. They come again when the folders change; else saidBefore names them. fetch { slicer: "orcaslicer", vendors: ["BBL", "Prusa" …], version } downloads OrcaSlicer's system presets of the same version as JSON. version: only three numbers, such as 2.3.1. Other text is refused. fetch needs the network; OrcaSlicer packs its own where they cannot be read. use { body, machine, process, filament } (names from list) or { body, bundle } puts them on the print setup of the body. The layer height, walls, infill and shells of the setup then come from the presets (settingsFromPresets), and slice uses them. use writes the setup. export { machine, process, filament | bundle | body, path, name } writes one flattened JSON bundle and keeps it. import { path, name } keeps a bundle from a file. It needs Agent Link for OrcaSlicer installed. PrusaSlicer has no presets here: give slice_with profiles { config: an .ini }. Refused: no presets of that slicer on this computer. Refused: a name that is not found. Refused: use on a body in no print setup. Nothing of any printer is in the code: the presets are the authority. The answer by action: list { slicer, from, the presets by kind { count, own, presets, more }, saved, next, note, saidBefore }. use { setup, presets, slicer, settingsFromPresets, note }; export { exported (path), name, presets }; import { imported, kept, presets, next }.
slicer_presets.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

slice_with.description: Slice a body or a mesh in a print setup with a named slicer, by its command line. A mesh goes on the plate as it is, with no new triangles. That is a Mesh::Feature, such as the Textured object of texture_apply. It takes the print setup of its source body when it has none of its own. An object that is neither a solid nor a mesh is refused, by its type. slicer: prusaslicer (default), orcaslicer or bambustudio. profiles: { machine, process, filament } JSON file paths for OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio, or { config } an .ini for PrusaSlicer. Left out, it uses the presets of the setup (slicer_presets use). Else it writes minimal profiles from the setup, with the defaults of the slicer for the rest. Those are fine for a time and weight estimate, not for a real print. OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio also take more inputs. bodies [names]: several on one plate, arranged. orient and arrange: the slicer's own. overrides { the slicer's process keys }. project: true writes the sliced plate as a .3mf that its window opens; slice_open shows it. material: a filament id for this slice only, not recorded. A filament profile or the presets of the setup win over material. name: the base name of the files. Pauses for encased parts (hw_embed, the magnets of gen_make) are written after their layer. The pause is M601, Bambu's M400 U1, or pauseCommand. pauseCommand: only M601, M600, M0, M1 or PAUSE, one command, no new lines. There are no pauses with several bodies or orient: the heights are those of one body as modelled. Then warning names each pause dropped, and the call to keep it: slice that body alone, without orient. warning also says when a pause could not be placed. Refused: no print setup. Refused: the presets of the setup belong to another slicer. Refused: a profile path that is not a file. Refused: a profile path in a credentials or settings folder (as Agent Link refuses a read there). Refused: orient, arrange, project, overrides or several bodies with prusaslicer. Refused unavailable: a slicer not on this computer; the refusal names those present. AGENTLINK_ORCASLICER and AGENTLINK_BAMBUSTUDIO set their paths. It needs Agent Link for OrcaSlicer installed. Cost: a body is meshed at 0.01 mm deviation, then the slicer runs, from seconds to minutes. It runs as a job when long (job_status finishes it). The answer holds { body, slicer, exe, profiles, gcode, bytes, time, filament, layers, verdict, setup, bodies, project, pauses, pauseCommand, material, overrides, mesh, warning, note }. It also holds the slicer's warnings and plate statistics. profiles: which were used. gcode: the path. filament and layers: as read from the G-code. verdict: a few words with its time and filament ("12m 3s, 3.21 g"), else "G-code written". Starting the print is the call of the person.

material.description: A filament id for this slice only (not recorded).

slice_with.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

slice_read.description: Read back an OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio project (.3mf). It can be one that slice_with wrote (project: true). Or it can be one that the person changed and saved in the slicer's window. path: absolute, or relative to the folder of the session. The answer holds the slicer, the presets it names, and each setting changed from them (project-wide and per filament). It holds the own settings and modifier parts of every object, the plates, and the slicer's warnings. When the project holds a sliced plate, the answer holds its time, weight, cost and features. slice: true first slices the project as it stands (its own settings, headless; seconds to minutes). It then adds slicedNow { gcode, time, filament … }. Refused: no such file. Refused: not a slicer project. Refused: the slicer is not on this computer. Changes nothing in the document. To take a changed setting into the print setup, use slicer_presets or setup set.
slice_read.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

slice_open.description: Open a project (.3mf) in the slicer's own window, for the person. path: absolute, or relative to the folder of the session. slicer: orcaslicer (default) or bambustudio. The person changes what they like there and saves; slice_read then brings it back. It only starts the slicer and answers at once. It does not wait for the person or know when they are done: ask them. It needs the FreeCAD window (refused headless) and the slicer on this computer. The answer holds: opened (path), in, next.
slice_open.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

printer_add.description: Keep a printer on the network by name (1 to 40 characters). kind octoprint: key (its API key) is required. kind moonraker or klipper: key only if it asks for one. kind prusalink: key, or user and password for its digest login. url: its address (http:// is assumed). It is kept in ~/AgentLink/printers.json (owner only), never in the folder of the session. An old .agentlink-printers.json in the session folder moves there once. No tool ever gives the key and password back. The same name again replaces it. It is tried at once (check: false skips that). An address off this network is not tried unless check is true. That is an address that is not private and not a .local name. warning says so. warning also says when plain http sends the key in clear text. The answer then holds reached true with state, or reached false with why; it is kept either way. Bambu Lab printers are refused. They take jobs only over their own LAN protocol or from Bambu Studio. Use slice_with { slicer: "bambustudio" }, then send from there. Never ask the person to paste a key into a chat that they do not trust. A key is theirs to give. The answer holds: added { name, kind, url, how it logs in }, replaced, kept (the file), warning, reached, state | why. Changes nothing in the document.
printer_add.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

printer_list.description: List the printers that printer_add keeps: printers [{ name, kind, url, how it logs in }]. It never gives the keys. remove: a name; it forgets that printer, and the answer adds removed. A name that is not kept is refused, with a list of those that are. Changes nothing in the document.
printer_list.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

printer_status.description: Read the state of a printer now, over the network. printer: its name from printer_add; you can leave it out when one is kept. The answer holds: printer, kind, state, nozzle { now, target } and bed { now, target } °C, job { file, progress % , and time left or printed where the printer gives it }. state is the printer's own word: idle, printing, paused, error …. Refused: no printer is kept. Refused: the name is not kept. Refused: the printer does not answer (its address, key, or it is off). The text from the printer is cleaned (no invisible characters) and capped. A redirect to another host is refused. Changes nothing.

printer.description: The printer's name, as printer_add kept it; may be left out when there is one.

printer_status.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

printer_send.description: Upload a G-code file to a printer. file (required): an absolute path or a name in the folder of the session (.gcode, .gco, .g, .bgcode). slice and slice_with write it. A file in a credentials or settings folder is refused. printer: you can leave it out when one is kept. storage: where on the printer. Only local or sdcard for OctoPrint, gcodes for Moonraker, usb or local for PrusaLink (the first when left out). The tool reads the whole file first. It looks for commands that change the printer: firmware, settings, power, endstops. It looks for motors off while the print moves. It looks for heat over the caps (nozzle 300 °C, bed 120 °C). It is uploaded and NOT started. Starting needs start: true and the approval of the person. A file with such commands also needs the approval of the person, with or without start. With Agent Link, the first call answers pending with the approve_file arguments. They name the printer, the action and the file with its sha256. Call approve_file with them, then call this tool again with the same arguments. The person sets approve_file in the client's tool permissions. The tool never approves by itself. A typed confirm is refused with Agent Link. confirm ("start <printer name>", or "send <printer name>" for a file with such commands) is only for Workshop without Agent Link. Never start a print on your own. With start, it is refused while the printer is printing, paused or busy. The answer holds: uploaded, where, started, printer, bytes, sha256, issues, note. Or pending, approve, next, issues.

printer.description: The printer's name, as printer_add kept it; may be left out when there is one.

storage.description: Where on the printer: local or sdcard (OctoPrint), gcodes (Moonraker), usb or local (PrusaLink). The first by default.

printer_send.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 25bafcb (moved to Workshop Make)

printer_pause.description: Pause the running job of the printer. It needs the approval of the person. With Agent Link, the first call answers pending with the approve_file arguments (the printer and the action). Call approve_file with them, then call this tool again. The person sets approve_file in the client's tool permissions. The tool never approves by itself. A typed confirm is refused with Agent Link. confirm: "pause <printer name>", word for word, only for Workshop without Agent Link. That is the call of the person: ask them first. printer: you can leave it out when one is kept. Refused: no approval, or the printer does not answer. The answer holds: printer, and what the printer answered. Or pending, approve, next.

printer.description: The printer's name, as printer_add kept it; may be left out when there is one.

printer_stop.description: Stop (cancel) the job of the printer. It cannot be resumed, and the print is lost. It needs the approval of the person, every time. With Agent Link, the first call answers pending with the approve_file arguments (the printer and the action). Call approve_file with them, then call this tool again. The person sets approve_file in the client's tool permissions. The tool never approves by itself. A typed confirm is refused with Agent Link. confirm: "stop <printer name>", word for word, only for Workshop without Agent Link. That is the call of the person: ask them first, every time. printer: you can leave it out when one is kept. Refused: no approval, or the printer does not answer. The answer holds: printer, and what the printer answered. Or pending, approve, next.

cut_check.description: Check if a body in a cut setup can be cut from sheet. It must be a sheet part: two parallel flat faces a constant thickness apart. Every other face must be square to them. The faces that are not square are named under sheet.notSquare and sheet.steps. Then it checks, for the machine (laser, waterjet, plasma, router), material and thickness. It checks its thickness against the sheet of the setup. It checks holes, webs (material left between cuts) and slots under the least feature. It checks inside corners of a router tighter than its cutter, and plasma holes under the thickness. It checks the part against the sheet [w, h]. machine, material and sheet given here override those of the cut setup for this check. Materials: steel, stainless, aluminium, brass, copper, titanium, acrylic, plywood, wood, mdf, hdpe, polycarbonate, cardboard, rubber, foam, carbon. When neither says, steel is assumed, and plywood on a router. Refused: the body is in no cut setup (setup add { type: "cut" } first). Refused: the body has no flat face. The answer holds { body, verdict, machine, material, kerf, sheet { thickness, normal }, profile { size [x, y], holes, edges, leastWeb, leastGap }, least, findings, setup, unjudged, assumed, note }. verdict: fix | pass with warnings | pass. least: the limits used. findings [{ rule (not-sheet, thickness, small-hole, thin-web, narrow-slot, inside-corner, sheet-size), severity, value, limit, at, says }]: the first 10. unjudged: sheet size, when no sheet is given. assumed: what the setup left out (machine laser, material, kerf, thickness). The least features are rules of thumb; the figures of the cutting shop win. Webs are not read on a profile of over 160 edges (assumed says so). Changes nothing.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

cut_check.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 5b1bbde (moved to Workshop Make)

cut_export.description: Write the flat profiles of sheet bodies as DXF and SVG in mm, laid out on a sheet. The files go to the folder of the session. body, or bodies [names] (the one body when left out), each in a cut setup. copies: n, or { "body label": n } (1 to 500). sheet: [w, h] (the sheet of the cut setup when left out). gap: mm between parts and from the edge (3 mm or two kerfs). formats: ["dxf", "svg"] (both when left out). name: the base name of the files. With a sheet, FreeCAD's BIM nesting places the parts (the module of Arch_Nest); parts are never turned. nest: false, no sheet, or no BIM lays them in rows instead; layout says which and why. Parts that do not fit are counted under left. compensate: true offsets each outline out and each hole in by half the kerf. Leave it off when the software of the cutter does that. DXF is R12 (LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, POLYLINE) on layers OUTER and HOLES. Each file is read back and counted (readBack, matches). One thickness per file: bodies of another thickness are refused. Refused too: a body is not a sheet part (cut_check says why). Refused too: nothing fits the sheet. Nesting many copies of an intricate outline can take a minute or more: export fewer copies per call. The answer holds: files { dxf { path, bytes, readBack, layers, matches }, svg { path, bytes, readBack } }, placed { body: n }, left, sheet, thickness, kerf, compensated, gap, entities, layout, note. It writes files only; the document is not changed.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

nest.description: Lay the parts out with FreeCAD's BIM Nest when a sheet is given (true by default).

cut_export.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 5b1bbde (moved to Workshop Make)

tube_cutlist.description: Write a cut list for a weldment of round tubes, as markdown and CSV in the output folder. Give members [{ name, from, to, od, wall }] in mm, from and to on the centre line. Or give bodies: straight round tube bodies, modelled node to node. An end meets a tube whose centre line is within its outside radius plus tol (1 mm by default). ends { tube: { from, to } } says it: the name of the tube it meets, or "square". Each tube gets od, wall, centreLength and cutLength. cutLength is between the long points of the copes. Each coped end gets meets, includedAngle, notcherAngle (0 for a square joint) and copeDepth. phase is the turn of the to-end cope from the from-end cope about the tube's axis, 0 to 180 degrees. The answer holds: tubes, stock (cut length by od x wall), files { markdown, csv }, warnings, note. Copes are against the receiving tube's outside diameter. The tool does not change the document.

members.description: The tubes: [{ name, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], od, wall, ends? }], mm.

bodies.description: Straight round tube bodies, by name.

ends.description: { tube name: { from, to } }: the tube each end meets, or "square".

tol.description: How far off a tube's outside an end can be and still meet it, mm (1).

mill_check.description: Check if a body in a mill setup can be milled. It finds faces that no tool direction reaches (undercuts, named), and faces past the reach of the tool. It finds inside corners tighter than the least tool can leave. It finds holes and pockets past the reach, or over 4 times as deep as wide. It finds walls too thin for the material, and it checks the stock. directions: the sides the tool comes from ("+z", "-x" …). Left out, directions are the axes of the setup ("3": +z only; "3+2": all six). tool: the diameter of the least end mill, mm (the minTool of the setup, else 3). reach: mm (5 x tool or 20). material: aluminium, steel, stainless, brass, copper, titanium, plastic, pom, wood (aluminium when left out). stock: [x, y, z] mm as the part stands. Left out, stock is the box of the part + 2 mm a side and 1 mm top and bottom. Refused: the body is in no mill setup (setup add { type: "mill" } first). The answer holds: body, verdict (fix | pass with warnings | pass), directions, tool, reach, material, stock, findings [{ rule, severity, says, faces }] (the first 10), leastWall, setup, grade, assumed. assumed: every value that the setup or the call left out, in words. Trap: a face on the outside of the stock counts as the stock's own. Faces are sampled, so a small undercut between samples can be missed. Face names change after any edit. Changes nothing; heavy on bodies with many faces.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

directions.description: Sides the tool comes from; by default the setup's axes: 3 is +z, 3+2 all six.

tool.description: The least end mill's diameter, mm (the setup's minTool).

reach.description: How deep the tool reaches, mm.

material.description: aluminium, aluminum, steel, stainless, brass, copper, titanium, plastic, pom, wood

stock.description: [x, y, z] mm, as the part stands.

mill_check.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 5b1bbde (moved to Workshop Make)

mill_export.description: Write the STEP file of a milled body and its setup sheet to the folder of the session. The STEP file is read back and compared. It takes the inputs of mill_check (directions, tool, reach, material, stock) and runs that check first. name: the base name of the files. cam: true (the default) uses FreeCAD's CAM. A CAM Job that already holds the body is used again as it is. Else a NEW Job is added to the document, with a box stock and the least tool used here. This changes the document: a Job, its stock, model clone and tool controller, in one undo step. CAM's own Sanity report (HTML) is then the setup sheet. Make's mill check is added to it (verdict, findings, least wall, what was assumed). A new Job has no operations: add them with the cam_ tools. The window is left as it was. CAM's Sanity report hides every object to take its pictures, and puts back only part of them. So each object of the document is shown or hidden again as before the call. camJob.shownAgain: how many were put back. The box stock and tool model of a new Job are hidden, as CAM's own Job leaves them. The stock shows with CAM's job tools. cam: false, or a CAM failure, writes Make's own Markdown sheet instead, and camNote says why. Nothing is then added to the document. Refused: the body is in no mill setup. The answer holds: body, verdict, step { path, bytes, volumeDiff, solids }, findings (how many), setupSheet { path, bytes, by }, camJob { label, reused, note, shownAgain }, camNote. volumeDiff: mm³ between the STEP read back and the body. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

body.description: A body's name; may be left out when there is one.

directions.description: Sides the tool comes from; by default the setup's axes: 3 is +z, 3+2 all six.

tool.description: The least end mill's diameter, mm (the setup's minTool).

reach.description: How deep the tool reaches, mm.

material.description: aluminium, aluminum, steel, stainless, brass, copper, titanium, plastic, pom, wood

stock.description: [x, y, z] mm, as the part stands.

cam.description: Use FreeCAD's CAM for the Job and setup sheet (true by default).

fea_frame.description: Solve a frame of straight members with beam elements (CalculiX B32): beams, rafters, portal frames, trusses, shelving. It is a sizing look, not a sign-off. Joints are rigid, and connections are not designed. members [{ name, from [x, y, z], to [x, y, z] mm, section { kind rect (b, d) | circ (d) | pipe (d, t) | box (b, d, t) } mm, material }]. Or bodies [labels]: box-like members. Their centre line, width and depth are read from their shape (rect sections). For an upright member, the larger of the two cross sizes is taken as depth. material: an id from material_list for all members, or per member. It must have a Young's modulus. supports (required) [{ at [x, y, z] a member's end, kind pinned | fixed | roller }]. at must be within tolerance mm of an end (1, or the largest section size with bodies). loads [{ member, w: N/mm downward (or [wx, wy, wz]) } | { member, kPa, width mm (1000) } | { at [x, y, z] a joint, force [fx, fy, fz] N }]. gravity: true adds own weight (−z). elements: per member (8). deflectionLimit (for example 360) judges span over deflection. timeout: s (300). name: the name of the folder of the study. Refused: CalculiX (ccx) not found; set its path in FEM's preferences or AGENTLINK_CCX. Refused: no members, or no supports. Refused: an unknown section kind or material. Refused: a member end that is not [x, y, z]. It runs as a job: seconds for a small frame; job_status finishes a longer one. Changes nothing in the document: the input deck and results are files in the folder of the session. The answer holds { members, supports [{ at, kind, reactionN }], loadTotalN, loadN, reactionsNote, files, worst, verdict, bodies, elements, note }. loadN: its size, one number. files: the folder of the study. worst: the member with the least safety. members [{ member, length, axialBendingMPa [min, max], vonMisesMPa, safety, deflectionMm, spanOverDeflection, deflectionOk, movesMm }]. safety: yield over von Mises, where the material has a yield. deflectionMm: across the member, from the line between its ends. reactionsNote: when CalculiX reads the reactions short of the load. verdict: a few words ("least safety 2.4, Rafter", or below 1 "past yield: safety 0.8, Post"). Where no material gives a yield, verdict gives the largest stress. bodies: the labels of the bodies it was made from, when given. More: guide_read { topic: "frame" }.
fea_frame.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 5b1bbde (moved to Workshop Make)
